facts.title: high potential incident - pressure exposure at TK-7104

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage was never verified as effective, and the learning team review classified this as an organisational factor.

Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels was in place but did not perform, and the learning team review classified this as an individual or team action.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the integrity of the mechanical seal support system on TK-7104 and LT-7104 and record the assurance activity before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in responding to a loss of containment, specifically isolating and depressuring a leaking system. TK-7104 (product storage tanks) is in service for export product storage. The task proceeded during transfer operations while the secondary containment by bund and drainage was never verified as effective. The pressure energy involved is held as hydraulic accumulator, and the recorded presentation was jet release, stored-energy discharge, rupture.
response.summary: On 20 April 2024 a high potential incident was recorded on TK-7104 and LT-7104 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during transfer operations; pressure energy held as hydraulic accumulator was not released.
